Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Article-specific behavioural hunt — A tale of two eras
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Talos prevalent-malware IOC hit: Coinminer/Injector/Dropper hashes + VID001.exe lure · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Talos prevalent-malware IOC hit: Coinminer/Injector/Dropper hashes + VID001.exe lure AIInstallation High
Hunts for the four SHA256/MD5 hashes Talos published in the 2026-06-11 Threat Source newsletter as the most prevalent malware files in their telemetry that week (Win.Worm.Coinminer, W32.Injector, Win.Dropper.Miner), plus the example lure filename VID001.exe. Article-specific — these are concrete, freshly-curated reputation hits from a Tier-1 vendor's weekly telemetry, not a generic miner template. Rationale: Uses the four SHA256 hashes (9f1f11..., 96fa6a..., a31f22..., 9896a6...), four MD5 hashes (2915b3..., aac316..., 7bdbd1..., 38de5b...) and the lure filename VID001.exe published verbatim in the Talos newsletter as their weekly prevalent-malware roundup. Talos detection names (Win.Worm.Coinminer::1201, W32.Injector:Gen.21ie.1201, Win.Dropper.Miner::95.sbx.tg) provide secondary corroboration; the hashes are themselves Talos-authoritative IOCs so no external second source is required. Combines reviewer suggestions #1 (Coinminer/VID001.exe) and #2 (W32.Injector) into a single hash-IOC match since the article provides no behavioural detail beyond the hashes. Cross-checked against: • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974 • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1496 T1055
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware analyst workstation detonating these specific samples in a sandbox VM (filter on dedicated malware-lab device groups)
  • Red-team or purple-team exercise that seeded public Talos IOCs as known-bad payloads for control validation
  • Threat-intel ingestion pipeline (e.g. MISP/ThreatFox sync) writing the sample files into a quarantined research share but never executing them — generates DeviceFileEvents hits without process execution
  • AV/EDR engine itself quarantining the file and emitting a hash-tagged action event that downstream telemetry shippers re-log
  • Sample harvested by EDR scheduled scans of mounted forensic images (DFIR workstation reviewing a prior incident)
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in~ (dynamic(["MALWARE-LAB-01","DFIR-WS-01","SANDBOX-DETONATE-01"])) and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","falcon-sensor.exe","CSFalconService.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: confirm the hit is on a real production endpoint (not a sandbox/DFIR/red-team device); pull the full process tree for the matching SHA256/MD5/VID001.exe execution, the parent process, and the originating file write to identify the delivery vector (browser download, email attachment, USB, SMB share). Contain: isolate the endpoint via Defender/Falcon network containment, block the SHA256 hashes via custom IOC indicator (Defender CIM / Falcon IOC Management), and quarantine any DeviceFileEvents copies still on disk. Hunt: pivot on the parent process and download URL/email to find other recipients that received the same lure but haven't executed yet; sweep DeviceNetworkEvents from infected hosts for mining-pool traffic (stratum+tcp://, common ports 3333/4444/5555/7777/14444) and other beaconing not blocked by network containment; check DeviceImageLoadEvents for unsigned DLLs loaded by the injector sample to map post-exploitation persistence.
let TalosHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91"]);
let TalosMd5 = dynamic(["2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376","38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98"]);
union
( DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where SHA256 in (TalosHashes) or MD5 in (TalosMd5) or FileName =~ "VID001.exe" or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (TalosHashes) or InitiatingProcessMD5 in (TalosMd5)
  | project Timestamp, Source="Process", DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
),
( DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where SHA256 in (TalosHashes) or MD5 in (TalosMd5) or FileName =~ "VID001.exe"
  | project Timestamp, Source="FileWrite", DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
)
| order by Timestamp desc

let TalosMd5 = dynamic(["2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376","38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98"]);

title: Talos Weekly Prevalent Malware IOC Hit (2026-06-11)
id: 5f1c6e0e-2d4b-4c2a-9d8e-1a2b3c4d5e6f
description: Detects execution or write of files matching SHA256/MD5 hashes or the VID001.exe filename published by Cisco Talos as their most-prevalent-malware list in the 2026-06-11 Threat Source newsletter (Win.Worm.Coinminer, W32.Injector, Win.Dropper.Miner).
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/a-tale-of-two-eras/
  - https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:

  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1496
  - attack.t1055
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_hash_sha256:
    Hashes|contains:
      - '9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507'
      - '96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974'
      - 'a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91'
  selection_hash_md5:

      - '2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f'
      - 'aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9'
      - '7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376'
      - '38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98'
  selection_filename:
    Image|endswith: '\VID001.exe'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Malware reverse-engineering or sandbox detonation labs running these specific samples for analysis
  - Internal red-team exercises seeded with public IOCs
level: high

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_hash IN ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91","2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376","38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") OR Processes.process_name="VID001.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_hash Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] OpenClaw agent outbound to Imperva PoC domain imperva_artifactory.com · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] OpenClaw agent process spawns script interpreter or download LOLBin · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] AI agent mailbox auto-forward of credentials or bulk customer data to external recipient · [LLM] AI agent process reads cloud credential stores or .env secrets before egress · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
OpenClaw agent outbound to Imperva PoC domain imperva_artifactory.com AIDelivery High
Detects any host or AI-agent process reaching out to imperva_artifactory.com, the researcher-controlled domain used by Imperva's PoC to host the script the prompt-injected OpenClaw agent downloads and executes. Hunts the indicator-of-compromise from the article rather than a generic LOLBin pattern. Rationale: Uses the article's only hard IOC — imperva_artifactory.com — the Imperva researchers' PoC host serving the script downloaded by the prompt-injected agent. Pivot is a single-string IOC match across DNS / proxy / EDR network paths; FP rate is essentially zero outside of security researchers.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher or red team intentionally testing the Imperva PoC
  • Threat-intel feed crawler resolving the domain for IOC enrichment
  • Imperva customers running sanctioned demos of the disclosure
  • Internal AI-security training labs replaying the PoC
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("threatintel-collector.exe","vt-uploader.exe")
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the calling process and command line — confirm whether the requester is an OpenClaw / AI-agent runtime (openclaw, python, node, electron) and identify the user/container context. Check whether any file was written or executed in the seconds after the connect. 2. Contain: block imperva_artifactory.com at the proxy/EDR, isolate the host running the agent, and revoke any credentials the agent had access to (AWS IAM keys, mailbox tokens). 3. Hunt: search 7 days back for the same domain across the org and look for other AI-agent hosts that ingested shared contacts/vCards/location pins in the same window; verify OpenClaw is patched to 2026.4.23+.
let openclaw_procs = dynamic(["openclaw.exe","openclaw","python.exe","python3","node.exe","node","electron.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "imperva_artifactory.com" or RemoteUrl endswith ".imperva_artifactory.com"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
(union isfuzzy=true
    (DnsEvents
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where Name has "imperva_artifactory.com"
     | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, ClientIP, Query=Name, Source="DnsEvents"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where RequestURL has "imperva_artifactory.com" or DestinationHostName has "imperva_artifactory.com" or DestinationDnsDomain has "imperva_artifactory.com"
     | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Query=coalesce(RequestURL, DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain), Source="CommonSecurityLog"),
    (ImDnsActivity
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where DnsQuery has "imperva_artifactory.com"
     | project TimeGenerated, Host=SrcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Query=DnsQuery, Source="ImDnsActivity")
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: OpenClaw Agent Outbound to Imperva PoC Domain imperva_artifactory.com
id: 8b7a4d2c-5c0e-4f0a-9a3a-2b1c6e8f9d10
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS or HTTP traffic to imperva_artifactory.com, the PoC domain Imperva used to stage the script that prompt-injected OpenClaw agents downloaded and executed.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-attacks-trick-openclaw-ai-agent.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: dns
product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|contains: 'imperva_artifactory.com'
  condition: selection
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd OR source:cloudtrail OR source:windows.defender) (@DestinationHostname:*imperva_artifactory.com* OR @network.destination.name:*imperva_artifactory.com* OR @QueryName:*imperva_artifactory.com* OR @dns.question.name:*imperva_artifactory.com*)
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/imperva_artifactory\.com/i) OR (#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/(openclaw|python|node|electron)/i) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_ip) as dest_ip values(All_Traffic.app) as proc from datamodel=Network_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest="imperva_artifactory.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.imperva_artifactory.com" by All_Traffic.src host All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_ip) as dest_ip values(All_Traffic.app) as proc from datamodel=Network_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest="imperva_artifactory.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.imperva_artifactory.com" by All_Traffic.src host All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OpenClaw agent process spawns script interpreter or download LOLBin AIExploitation Medium
Hunts for the OpenClaw runtime (or comparable self-hosted AI agents) spawning a script interpreter or download utility — the on-host signal of the Imperva PoC where a hidden instruction in a shared contact / vCard / location label drove the agent to fetch and execute attacker code. Pivots on the parent being an agent process rather than a generic interpreter launch. Rationale: Pivots on the Imperva PoC outcome — the OpenClaw agent downloading and running a script after ingesting a poisoned contact/vCard/location. Parent-process narrow (agent runtime) + child-LOLBin + network/decode argument is the high-fidelity combination per the KQL anti-bare-process-execution rule.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.006 T1105 T1204.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate OpenClaw plugin that wraps PowerShell/curl for a sanctioned task
  • Developer iterating on an OpenClaw tool that shells out
  • Electron-based AI assistant updating itself via PowerShell installer
  • Python-based agent invoking curl for a vetted MCP server install
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("openclaw-installer","openclaw-update","npm install","pip install") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("npmjs.org","pypi.org","github.com/openclaw"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the full parent/child cmdline and the URL/file the child interacted with — confirm it's not a sanctioned agent plugin and check the source message/contact that triggered the action. 2. Contain: kill the child process, suspend the agent runtime, and isolate the host. Block any external URL/IP touched. 3. Hunt: review the agent's recent message inputs for hidden text in contact-name / vCard / location-label fields; confirm OpenClaw is on 2026.4.23+; sweep other agent hosts for the same parent→child→URL chain.
let agent_parents = dynamic(["openclaw.exe","openclaw","electron.exe","node.exe","node","python.exe","python3","pwsh.exe"]);
let child_lolbins = dynamic(["powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash","sh","zsh"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (agent_parents)
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("openclaw","open-claw","openclaw-runtime","openclaw-agent")
| where FileName in~ (child_lolbins)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","DownloadString","Invoke-WebRequest","IEX","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","curl ","wget ","-c ","-Command","-NoProfile","-ExecutionPolicy","Bypass")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let agent_parents = dynamic(["openclaw.exe","openclaw","electron.exe","node.exe","node","python.exe","python3","pwsh.exe"]);
let child_lolbins = dynamic(["powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash","sh","zsh"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any (agent_parents)
    or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("openclaw","open-claw","openclaw-runtime","openclaw-agent")
| where ActingProcessName has_any (child_lolbins)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","DownloadString","Invoke-WebRequest","IEX","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","curl ","wget ","-c ","-Command","-NoProfile","-ExecutionPolicy","Bypass")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = ActingProcessName, ChildCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AI agent mailbox auto-forward of credentials or bulk customer data to external recipient AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Varonis 'agent phishing' outcome — the OpenClaw-class agent reading a single inbound mail and shipping AWS keys / DB strings / SSH creds / a bulk customer export to an external Gmail address. Looks for app-driven Send/Forward where the body or attachment carries secret-shaped tokens and the recipient is outside the org. Rationale: Targets the Varonis Pinchy scenario verbatim — agent reading a normal-looking mail and forwarding mock AWS IAM keys, DB connection strings, SSH credentials, or a 247-customer export to an outside Gmail. Combines outbound-to-personal-mail recipients with secret-token regexes and the article's exact pretext subjects ('staging access', 'weekly customer export', 'QBR').
ATT&CKT1567 T1114.003 T1552.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sales engineer legitimately sending a customer summary to a partner's Gmail
  • Sysadmin emailing themselves a sanitised connection string for travel
  • Finance/Legal exchanging customer lists with external auditors
  • User forwarding their own AWS sandbox keys to a personal address (still policy-violating but not the article's TTP)
Suppression filter
| where not (UserAgent has_any ("Outlook","Mail/","Thunderbird") and isempty(strcat("openclaw","pinchy")))
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the original inbound trigger mail (sender, urgency cues, pretext) and the outbound mail's body/attachments. Confirm whether send was initiated by the OpenClaw / Pinchy agent identity or the human user. 2. Contain: recall the message via O365 / Vault, rotate every secret it contained (AWS keys, DB passwords, SSH keys), suspend the agent's mailbox connector, and require human approval for outbound mail. 3. Hunt: search 30d for other agent-driven sends to free-mail recipients; map the agent's connector access vs. the trust level of the triggering input (Varonis control #3); apply the four Varonis controls (policy-enforced instructions, outbound mail gate, connector trust-scoped to trigger, human-in-loop for credentials).
let internal_domains = dynamic(["contoso.com","yourcorp.com"]);
let secret_markers = dynamic(["AKIA","ASIA","aws_access_key_id","aws_secret_access_key","BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY","BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY","ssh-rsa","postgres://","mysql://","mongodb://","jdbc:","-----BEGIN"]);
let agent_subjects = dynamic(["staging access","production incident","weekly customer export","QBR","credentials","customer list","enterprise customers"]);
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where EmailDirection in ("Outbound","Intra-org")
| where not(RecipientEmailAddress has_any (internal_domains))
| where Subject has_any (agent_subjects)
   or AdditionalFields has_any (secret_markers)
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderObjectId,
          RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, AttachmentCount, UrlCount,
          DeliveryAction, AdditionalFields
| join kind=leftouter (
    CloudAppEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)

  ) on $left.SenderObjectId == $right.AccountObjectId
| where UserAgent has_any ("openclaw","OpenClaw","Pinchy","langchain","gemini","codex","node-fetch","python-requests","axios")
   or isempty(UserAgent)
| order by Timestamp desc

let secret_markers = dynamic(["AKIA","ASIA","aws_access_key_id","aws_secret_access_key","BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY","BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY","ssh-rsa","postgres://","mysql://","mongodb://","jdbc:","-----BEGIN"]);
let agent_subjects = dynamic(["staging access","production incident","weekly customer export","QBR","credentials","customer list","enterprise customers"]);
OfficeActivity

| where Operation in~ ("Send","SendAs","SendOnBehalf","Forward","New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule")

AI agent process reads cloud credential stores or .env secrets before egress AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the precursor to the Varonis exfil scenario — an OpenClaw / Pinchy-style agent process (python/node/electron/openclaw) reading .aws/credentials, .env, id_rsa, or HKCU credential keys, immediately followed by outbound network to an external host. Targets the file-access → exfil chain the article's 'leaking secrets' headline describes. Rationale: Targets the 'leaking secrets' Varonis path — the agent reading .aws/credentials, .env, ssh keys, then talking to an external host within 5 minutes. Time-window join on (DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId) keeps the signal high-fidelity vs bare file-read or bare egress hunts, per the KQL anti-single-table-when-correlation-needed rule.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1041
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running an AI coding assistant that legitimately reads .env to bootstrap a project
  • openclaw-update or pip/npm package post-install that touches credential files for migration
  • AWS CLI auto-refresh kicked by a python agent under sanctioned automation
  • Backup tool inventorying dotfiles right before scheduled sync
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("aws configure","aws sso login","gcloud auth") and RemoteUrl has_any ("amazonaws.com","googleapis.com"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm whether the read was prompted by an external input (vCard, contact name, location pin, email body) and capture the exact secret path + bytes egressed. Identify the destination IP/domain. 2. Contain: rotate the leaked credentials (AWS IAM, SSH, DB), revoke the agent's filesystem connector on .aws/.ssh/.env paths, isolate the host. 3. Hunt: pivot on the destination IP for other org hosts; sweep for the same agent process touching other secret stores (Keychain, Credential Manager, gcloud, kube); ensure OpenClaw 2026.4.23+ is enforced and the Varonis connector-trust control is in place.
let agent_procs = dynamic(["openclaw.exe","openclaw","electron.exe","node.exe","node","python.exe","python3","pwsh.exe"]);
let secret_paths = dynamic([@"\.aws\credentials","/.aws/credentials",@"\.aws\config","/.aws/config",@"\.env","/.env",@"\.ssh\id_rsa","/.ssh/id_rsa",@"\.ssh\id_ed25519",@"\.kube\config",@"\.azure\accessTokens.json",@"\.config\gcloud\credentials.db",@"\.netrc"]);
let FileReads = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (agent_procs)
    | where FolderPath has_any (secret_paths)
        or FileName in~ ("credentials",".env","id_rsa","id_ed25519","accessTokens.json")
    | project FileTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName,
              InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName,
              InitiatingProcessAccountName;
FileReads
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (agent_procs)
    | where RemoteIPType == "Public"
    | project NetTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId,

| where NetTime between (FileTime .. FileTime + 5m)
| project FileTime, NetTime,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', NetTime, FileTime),
          DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          SecretPath = strcat(FolderPath, "\\", FileName),
          RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by FileTime desc
let agent_procs = dynamic(["openclaw.exe","openclaw","electron.exe","node.exe","node","python.exe","python3","pwsh.exe"]);
let secret_paths = dynamic([@"\.aws\credentials","/.aws/credentials",@"\.aws\config","/.aws/config",@"\.env","/.env",@"\.ssh\id_rsa","/.ssh/id_rsa",@"\.kube\config",@"\.azure\accessTokens.json",@"\.netrc"]);

    | where DstIpAddr !startswith "10." and DstIpAddr !startswith "192.168." and DstIpAddr !startswith "172.16."

              DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkBytes

| project FileTime, NetTime,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', NetTime, FileTime),
          DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetFilePath, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkBytes
| order by FileTime desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |

    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a

author: Clankerusecase

detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'

    selection_domain:

        where Web.dest IN ("imperva_artifactory.com")

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)

   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

The Hacker News

Security researcher Chaotic Eclipse (aka Nightmare-Eclipse and MSNightmare) has released a new Windows BitLocker bypass dubbed GreatXML, a day after they published an exploit for Microsoft Defender. "This was an accidental discovery, it took a total of 4 hours to find this," the researcher said in a post on Blogger. "If you ever attempted to use Windows Defender Offline Scan, you're

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution

GreatXML staging: unattend.xml + ReAgent.xml dropped to Recovery partition root AIWeaponization High
Hunts the core GreatXML pre-boot staging artifact: a process writing 'unattend.xml' to the root of the recovery partition and 'ReAgent.xml' under a 'Recovery\WindowsRE\' path on that same volume. Combination is the signature step that primes WinRE for an unrestricted BitLocker-volume shell after a Shift+Restart boot. Rationale: Article explicitly names the two staging files and the exact relative path 'Recovery/WindowsRE/ReAgent.xml' written to the recovery partition root. Requiring BOTH file writes on the same host within a short window collapses FPs from normal ReAgent.xml maintenance (Windows updates touch only ReAgent.xml, never paired with an unattend.xml on the recovery volume). Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
ATT&CKT1542.005 T1112
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • MDT/SCCM-style OS provisioning workflows that stage unattend.xml on Recovery volume during imaging
  • OEM factory recovery image refresh that re-seeds Recovery\WindowsRE\ReAgent.xml during a Windows feature update
  • Acronis/Macrium Reflect recovery image creation writing ReAgent and unattend stubs
  • Sysprep cleanup tasks that legitimately drop unattend.xml in non-standard mount paths during golden image capture
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("dism.exe","sysprep.exe","setupact.exe","reagentc.exe","trustedinstaller.exe","sccm.exe","smsswd.exe","acronis_cloud.exe","reflect.exe")
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("services.exe","wuauclt.exe","tiworker.exe") and InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "reagentc.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the initiating process tree on the host; confirm whether the writer is a known imaging tool (sccm.exe, dism.exe, sysprep.exe, acronis*.exe) or an interactive shell/PowerShell session. Check whether MpCmdRun.exe initiated a Defender Offline Scan in the prior 48h (GreatXML prerequisite). 2) Contain: if no provisioning workflow is in flight, isolate the device, disable WinRE via `reagentc /disable`, and force a TPM/PIN BitLocker recovery key rotation on that volume before the next reboot. 3) Hunt: pivot on the writing account across other hosts for the same paired-file write within 7d; review any Shift+Restart / WinRE boot events in Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Boot/Operational. Escalate to IR if the host has high-value BitLocker-protected data.

reagentc.exe WinRE reconfiguration (setreimage / setosimage / boottore) AIInstallation High
Detects reagentc.exe being driven with flags that point WinRE at attacker-controlled images or force the next boot into the recovery environment. GreatXML requires a primed WinRE state so the planted XML pair is consumed on reboot, and operator-driven reagentc invocations outside patch/imaging workflows are the highest-fidelity precursor. Rationale: Article requires WinRE to be in a 'primed' (e.g., post offline-scan) state for the planted XML pair to be honoured. reagentc.exe is the only supported user-mode tool for /setreimage, /setosimage, and /boottore, and outside Windows servicing/imaging stacks these flags are almost never used legitimately - they directly stage the WinRE-side prerequisite GreatXML needs. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/reagentc-command-line-options
ATT&CKT1542.005 T1112
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT technician troubleshooting WinRE with `reagentc /setreimage` after a botched in-place upgrade
  • MDT/SCCM task sequence calling reagentc to re-point recovery image to a corporate WIM
  • OEM recovery refresh after a major Windows feature update
  • Help-desk-driven `reagentc /boottore` to capture user data ahead of a wipe-and-reload
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("sccm","smsswd","intune") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\CCM\", @"\MININT\", @"\Windows\Panther\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the operator account, parent process (interactive shell vs. SCCM/TI), and whether a change ticket exists for WinRE re-imaging. Check DeviceFileEvents on the same host for paired writes of unattend.xml + ReAgent.xml in the prior 30 minutes. 2) Contain: if no ticket, isolate the host before the next reboot - GreatXML triggers on WinRE entry. Cancel any pending boot-to-recovery via `reagentc /disable` then `reagentc /enable` once the WIM is verified. 3) Hunt: search 30-day reagentc.exe usage by the same account / cluster; correlate with MpCmdRun.exe `-OfflineScan` runs (article-cited prerequisite); review BitLocker key escrow for rotations matching these hosts.

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "reagentc.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/setreimage","/setosimage","/boottore"," boottore")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("tiworker.exe","trustedinstaller.exe","wuauclt.exe","setuphost.exe","sccm.exe","smsswd.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

title: Suspicious reagentc.exe WinRE Reconfiguration (GreatXML Precursor)
id: 1f8b6f0e-2b5a-4a8b-9e3c-7c6a1a44ad21
description: Detects reagentc.exe being invoked with flags that re-point WinRE at an attacker-controlled image or force-boot the next reboot into the recovery environment - the staging step described in the GreatXML BitLocker bypass.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1542.005
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith: '\reagentc.exe'
  selection_flags:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/setreimage'
      - '/setosimage'
      - '/boottore'
  filter_servicing:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\TiWorker.exe'
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\SetupHost.exe'
      - '\wuauclt.exe'
  condition: selection_image and selection_flags and not filter_servicing
level: high
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 @Image:(*\\reagentc.exe OR *\\Reagentc.exe OR *\\REAGENTC.EXE) @CommandLine:(*\/setreimage* OR *\/setosimage* OR *\/boottore*) -@ParentImage:(*\\TiWorker.exe OR *\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\wuauclt.exe OR *\\SetupHost.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\reagentc\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/(\/setreimage|\/setosimage|\/boottore)/i
| NOT (ParentBaseFileName=/^(TiWorker\.exe|TrustedInstaller\.exe|wuauclt\.exe|SetupHost\.exe)$/i)
| UserName!=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="reagentc.exe" AND (Processes.process="*/setreimage*" OR Processes.process="*/setosimage*" OR Processes.process="*/boottore*" OR Processes.process="* boottore*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(parent,"(?i)(TiWorker\.exe|TrustedInstaller\.exe|wuauclt\.exe|sccm.*\.exe)") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="reagentc.exe" AND (Processes.process="*/setreimage*" OR Processes.process="*/setosimage*" OR Processes.process="*/boottore*" OR Processes.process="* boottore*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(parent,"(?i)(TiWorker\.exe|TrustedInstaller\.exe|wuauclt\.exe|sccm.*\.exe)") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
Defender Offline Scan trigger (MpCmdRun -OfflineScan / BootSchedule) as GreatXML precursor AIWeaponization Medium
Article: 'If you ever attempted to use Windows Defender Offline Scan, you are automatically vulnerable to a BitLocker bypass.' Hunts hosts where MpCmdRun.exe scheduled or executed an offline scan, since this is the explicit precondition that primes WinRE for the GreatXML XML-drop attack. Rationale: The article calls out 'Defender Offline Scan ever initiated' as the necessary precondition for GreatXML, making MpCmdRun -OfflineScan / BootSchedule a high-value vulnerability inventory query. Joining against the unattend.xml/ReAgent.xml writes from UC1 lets analysts flag hosts that have both been primed AND staged. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/microsoft-defender-antivirus/command-line-arguments-microsoft-defender-antivirus
ATT&CKT1542.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • End user clicking 'Microsoft Defender Offline scan' from Windows Security UI after a malware alert (entirely legitimate but creates the same precondition)
  • SOC IR playbook that mandates an offline scan after EDR detections
  • Vendor remediation scripts that schedule an offline scan as part of cleanup
  • Sysadmin verifying offline-scan functionality on a freshly imaged host
Response runbook
1) Triage: treat hits as an asset-inventory feed rather than an alert - tag each device 'GreatXML-vulnerable'. Cross-reference with UC1 results to find devices that are BOTH primed (Defender offline) AND staged (XML pair planted). 2) Contain: for staged+primed hosts, enforce BitLocker pre-boot PIN where missing and rotate recovery keys; consider compensating control of disabling WinRE on high-value endpoints (`reagentc /disable`). 3) Hunt: review 90-day MpCmdRun.exe history; build a watchlist of vulnerable hosts so future XML-write alerts on those devices auto-escalate to high severity.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "MpCmdRun.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-OfflineScan","BootSchedule","-Scan -ScheduleJob -RestartMachine")
| summarize OfflineScanCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine), SampleAccount = any(InitiatingProcessAccountName)
            by DeviceName, DeviceId
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName in~ ("unattend.xml","ReAgent.xml")
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\Recovery\", @"\WindowsRE\", "HarddiskVolume")
    | summarize StagingArtifacts = make_set(FileName), StagingLastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceId
) on DeviceId
| extend Vulnerable = OfflineScanCount > 0, Staged = isnotempty(StagingArtifacts)
| project DeviceName, FirstSeen, LastSeen, OfflineScanCount, SampleAccount, SampleCmd, Vulnerable, Staged, StagingArtifacts, StagingLastSeen
| order by Staged desc, LastSeen desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\MpCmdRun.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("-OfflineScan", "BootSchedule", "-Scan -ScheduleJob -RestartMachine")
| summarize OfflineScanCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            SampleCmd = any(CommandLine), SampleAccount = any(AccountName)
            by Computer
| order by LastSeen desc
title: Windows Defender Offline Scan Initiated (GreatXML BitLocker Bypass Precondition)
id: 8d2a1b3e-9c7f-4a18-b6d2-5e0c2c1f9a44

WinRE-initiated cmd.exe with BitLocker volume access (post-exploit shell) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the post-exploitation result described in the article: a shell spawned inside WinRE with unrestricted access to a normally BitLocker-protected volume. Pivots on cmd.exe / X:\WINDOWS\System32 parentage and subsequent file enumeration of the protected C: drive from a winload/winre-context process. Rationale: Article describes the end-state as 'a shell spawned with unrestricted access to the BitLocker volume' inside WinRE. Process telemetry from inside the WinRE ramdisk (always X:\) is extremely rare in normal operations and is the cleanest single-pivot tell that the exploit succeeded and the attacker is now operating against the protected C: drive. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/windows-recovery-environment--windows-re--technical-reference
ATT&CKT1006 T1542.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin running diskpart/manage-bde from WinRE during a legitimate BitLocker recovery
  • Helpdesk-driven Startup Repair flows that fall back to a WinRE cmd.exe
  • OEM recovery-image utilities that surface a recovery shell during break-fix
  • MDT/SCCM in-place upgrade rollback that boots into WinRE for cleanup
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("StartupRepair","BootRec","WinRESetup") and DeviceName has_any ("-IT-","-LAB-","-IMG-"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm via change/ticket records whether the host was knowingly booted to WinRE; pull DeviceFileEvents to enumerate which BitLocker-protected files were touched from the X:\ context. Look for any file writes outward to USB / removable media (potential exfil of the protected volume). 2) Contain: physically secure the device, force a TPM reset and BitLocker key rotation; if evidence of data access, treat as a confirmed BitLocker bypass and escalate to IR + DPO. 3) Hunt: 90-day sweep for the same X:\ process pattern fleet-wide; correlate with UC1/UC2/UC3 to find hosts that were primed, staged, then executed.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith @"X:\" or FolderPath startswith @"X:\"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","notepad.exe","manage-bde.exe","reagentc.exe","diskpart.exe","robocopy.exe","xcopy.exe")
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith @"X:\"
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
    | where FolderPath !startswith @"X:\"
    | summarize TouchedFiles = make_set(FolderPath, 25), FileCount = count() by DeviceId
) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          TouchedFiles, FileCount
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName startswith @"X:\" or ParentProcessName startswith @"X:\"
| extend Bin = tostring(split(NewProcessName, @"\")[-1])
| where Bin in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","notepad.exe","manage-bde.exe","reagentc.exe","diskpart.exe","robocopy.exe","xcopy.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Process Execution from WinRE Volume (X:\) - GreatXML Post-Exploit Shell
id: e4a9f0d2-1b6b-4f2a-9e51-91c8a23c5d7e
description: Detects process creations where the image or parent image resolves to the WinRE ramdisk root (X:\). GreatXML lands the attacker in a cmd.exe inside WinRE with unrestricted access to the BitLocker-protected OS volume.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1542.005
  - attack.t1006
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    - Image|startswith: 'X:\'
    - ParentImage|startswith: 'X:\'
  filter_binary:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\notepad.exe'
      - '\manage-bde.exe'
      - '\reagentc.exe'
      - '\diskpart.exe'
      - '\robocopy.exe'
      - '\xcopy.exe'
  condition: selection and filter_binary
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(X\:\\Windows\\System32\\* OR X\:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\* OR X\:\\Sources\\*) OR @ParentImage:(X\:\\Windows\\System32\\* OR X\:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\*)) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\manage-bde.exe OR *\\reagentc.exe OR *\\diskpart.exe OR *\\robocopy.exe OR *\\xcopy.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/^X:\\/i OR ParentImageFileName=/^X:\\/i)
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|notepad|manage-bde|reagentc|diskpart|robocopy|xcopy)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, ParentImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_path) as parent_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_path="X:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\*" OR Processes.parent_process_path="X:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\*" OR Processes.process_path="X:\\Sources\\*") AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","notepad.exe","reagentc.exe","manage-bde.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_path) as parent_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_path="X:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\*" OR Processes.parent_process_path="X:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\*" OR Processes.process_path="X:\\Sources\\*") AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","notepad.exe","reagentc.exe","manage-bde.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45585")

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45585")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
