Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] FireAnt Metakit updater spawning script/LOLBin or writing PE to user-writable path (supply-chain)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — OceanLotus: From external espionage to domestic targeting
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER known-bad SHA1 hash on file write or process execution · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 callback to known infrastructure (IPs + domains) · [LLM] Sustained low-rate beaconing from single host to OceanLotus C2 IP set (long-tail intrusion signal) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 callback to known infrastructure (IPs + domains) AICommand & Control Medium
Detects outbound network connections or DNS resolutions to the specific C2 IPs and domains used by OceanLotus's SPECTRALVIPER backdoor across both the FireAnt Metakit supply-chain campaign and the 18-month construction-firm intrusion (mid-2024 - Feb 2026). Rationale: Uses the article's full C2 IOC table (Table 2 + IP/domain list) for the SPECTRALVIPER infrastructure. Both the early-2024-2026 construction-firm intrusion and the FireAnt supply-chain campaign reused subsets of this infrastructure, so any hit is article-grade. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platform / sandbox detonation lab that intentionally calls out to the same C2 IOCs for validation
  • Security researcher pivot/curl from a corporate analyst workstation
  • Stale Recorded Future/AlienVault enrichment job hitting these as 'check liveness' probes
  • DNS resolver cache poisoning resulting in legitimate domains briefly resolving to these IPs (very rare)
  • Honeypot or canary host deliberately deployed to attract OceanLotus traffic
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msftsbox.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Cisco\"
Response runbook
Step 1 - Triage: pull all DeviceProcessEvents on the source host for ±10 min around the hit; identify the InitiatingProcessFileName/FolderPath driving the connection and SHA1/SHA256 of that binary. Cross-check the hash against UC2 hash list and against the OS vendor. Step 2 - Contain: isolate the device in Defender, block the matched IP/domain at the proxy/EDR network-blocklist, suspend the user's AAD session, and snapshot RAM if forensics capacity exists - SPECTRALVIPER is memory-resident. Step 3 - Hunt: pivot on the parent process and any sibling processes; sweep the enterprise for the same SHA1/SHA256 and for connections to the entire OceanLotus IP/domain set in the last 90d; check FireAnt Metakit installs across the fleet.
let OceanLotusIPs = dynamic(["139.162.11.152","142.91.98.77","139.180.128.42","139.99.33.239","166.88.77.186","103.119.47.104","38.60.245.37","194.68.26.241"]);
let OceanLotusDomains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
union
( DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteIP in (OceanLotusIPs) or RemoteUrl has_any (OceanLotusDomains)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Source="DeviceNetworkEvents"
),
( DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
  | extend Q = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).query)
  | where Q has_any (OceanLotusDomains) or RemoteUrl has_any (OceanLotusDomains)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl=coalesce(RemoteUrl,Q), RemotePort, Source="DnsQueryResponse"
)
| order by Timestamp desc

SPECTRALVIPER known-bad SHA1 hash on file write or process execution AIInstallation High
Alerts on any file written or process executed whose SHA1 matches one of the 20 SPECTRALVIPER / OceanLotus loader/payload hashes published in the ESET report. Covers both the construction-firm campaign and the FireAnt Metakit supply-chain. Rationale: Pure hash IOC match against the 20 SHA1 values published in the ESET article. These are tied to confirmed SPECTRALVIPER samples (both old/reused and the heavily-obfuscated stable build per Table 1) - any hit on managed endpoints is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/software/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AV/EDR test lab intentionally executing the public SPECTRALVIPER samples for tuning
  • Threat-hunter who downloaded the samples from VT/MalwareBazaar onto a sandbox workstation
  • Incident-response forensic image being mounted/scanned on an analyst host
  • Sample triage by malware research team in a contained VLAN
  • Re-detection of the same artefact after a previous remediation that didn't purge backups
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in~ ("sandbox-01","malware-vm","ir-workstation") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Users\malware-analyst\"
Response runbook
Step 1 - Triage: confirm the host is not a sanctioned malware-analysis sandbox; pull the InitiatingProcessFileName and full ancestry; check whether the binary lives in %ProgramData%, %AppData%, %Temp%, or a FireAnt Metakit install dir (article-specific delivery vectors). Step 2 - Contain: isolate the device, force-quarantine the file via Defender, revoke any tokens/sessions for the AccountName, and snapshot memory before reboot - SPECTRALVIPER has orchestration capabilities and may have injected. Step 3 - Hunt: pivot to the C2 IOCs in UC1 from this host over the last 90d; enumerate every other endpoint with the same SHA1 in DeviceFileEvents (including non-executed file landings); check ASEPs / scheduled tasks / services created by the InitiatingProcess.

union

  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)

  | where SHA1 in (OceanLotusSHA1)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="DeviceImageLoadEvents"

FireAnt Metakit updater spawning script/LOLBin or writing PE to user-writable path (supply-chain) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for the FireAnt Metakit Vietnamese stock-investment client (Oct 2025 - Mar 2026 supply-chain compromise) acting as parent to script hosts, LOLBins, or writing PE/DLL payloads to %AppData%/%ProgramData%/%Temp% - the behaviour observed when its compromised update server delivered SPECTRALVIPER. Rationale: Article names FireAnt Metakit as the compromised Vietnamese stock-investment platform whose update server delivered SPECTRALVIPER from Oct 2025 to Mar 2026 (Table 1: 2025-10-02 first iteration / 2025-10-17 stable). Pivots on the FireAnt parent process - which should never legitimately spawn script hosts or download tools - plus PE drops to user-writable dirs. Both branches are article-specific. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate FireAnt auto-updater shelling out to PowerShell for post-install registration (low likelihood - most installers use msiexec)
  • Sysadmin troubleshooting a FireAnt crash by attaching cmd.exe via process explorer
  • FireAnt installer running NSIS uninstall script that legitimately calls cmd.exe
  • Endpoint security agent injecting a hook into FireAnt processes that appears as a child
  • Repackaged-by-IT MSI deployment running custom install scripts under a FireAnt context
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "-RegisterPackage" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--silent-install"
Response runbook
Step 1 - Triage: capture the FireAnt installation path + version, the child cmd-line in full, and SHA1 of both parent and child binaries; check whether the parent SHA1 matches UC2 list. Inventory FireAnt deployment fleet-wide via DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory. Step 2 - Contain: isolate the host, block FireAnt update-server FQDNs at the proxy until vendor confirms a clean build, freeze the user's brokerage/email sessions (stock-investor context = high-value target per article). Step 3 - Hunt: sweep all FireAnt hosts in the org for connections to the UC1 C2 IOCs over the same time window; check if FireAnt update files dropped on disk have non-vendor signatures or differ in size/hash from a known-good golden image; pivot to AccountName for any Vietnamese-domain user activity related to securities/financial-regulator topics.
let FireAntParents = dynamic(["fireant.exe","fireantmetakit.exe","metakit.exe","fireant_updater.exe","fireantupdater.exe"]);
let SuspChildren = dynamic(["powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msiexec.exe"]);
union
( DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (FireAntParents) or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit")
  | where FileName in~ (SuspChildren)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA1, Pivot="FireAnt_child_lolbin"
),
( DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (FireAntParents) or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit")
  | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
  | where FileName endswith ".exe" or FileName endswith ".dll" or FileName endswith ".scr" or FileName endswith ".lnk"
  | where FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\",@"\ProgramData\",@"\Temp\",@"\Public\")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256, Pivot="FireAnt_drops_PE"
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let FireAntParents = dynamic(["fireant.exe","fireantmetakit.exe","metakit.exe","fireant_updater.exe","fireantupdater.exe"]);
let SuspChildren = dynamic([@"\powershell.exe",@"\pwsh.exe",@"\cmd.exe",@"\mshta.exe",@"\wscript.exe",@"\cscript.exe",@"\rundll32.exe",@"\regsvr32.exe",@"\bitsadmin.exe",@"\certutil.exe",@"\curl.exe",@"\wget.exe",@"\msiexec.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any (FireAntParents) or ParentProcessName has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit")
| where NewProcessName has_any (SuspChildren)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType, Pivot="FireAnt_child_lolbin"
| union ( ImFileEvent
         | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
         | where ActingProcessName has_any (FireAntParents) or ActingProcessName has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit")
         | where TargetFileExtension in~ ("exe","dll","scr","lnk")
         | where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\AppData\",@"\ProgramData\",@"\Temp\",@"\Public\")
         | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, ParentProcessName=ActingProcessName, NewProcessName=TargetFilePath, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, TokenElevationType="", Pivot="FireAnt_drops_PE" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FireAnt Metakit Updater Spawning Script Host or LOLBin (OceanLotus Supply Chain)
id: 3a9f2b8c-5d4e-4c1f-bdf2-2e6a9c1d4f8a
description: Detects the FireAnt Metakit Vietnamese stock-trading client spawning script interpreters or LOLBins - the behaviour observed when OceanLotus's compromise of the FireAnt update server delivered SPECTRALVIPER to investor endpoints (Oct 2025 - Mar 2026).
references:

Sustained low-rate beaconing from single host to OceanLotus C2 IP set (long-tail intrusion signal) AICommand & Control Medium
Surfaces the 18-month construction-firm intrusion pattern (mid-2024 - Feb 2026): a single host with sustained, periodic, low-rate connections to one of the SPECTRALVIPER C2 IPs across many distinct hours and days. Tuned to catch the patient long-haul implant rather than a noisy beacon. Rationale: Article emphasises a 'prolonged espionage operation' (mid-2024 - Jan 2026, ~18 months) against a Vietnamese infrastructure & transport construction company - a low-rate sustained-presence shape. Statistical aggregation on the 8 published C2 IPs surfaces hosts with multi-day periodic contact, the long-tail signal the volumetric beaconing rules would miss. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1573
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security team running scheduled IOC-validation probes against the C2 IPs from a fixed scanning host
  • Threat-intel platform / Recorded Future / GreyNoise enrichment crawler hitting the same IPs
  • VPN concentrator or web proxy that aggregates all egress through one source IP (will look like sustained contact)
  • CDN/cloud-host customer who legitimately uses one of these IPs after OceanLotus moved off it (re-allocation)
  • Misconfigured SOC honeypot deployed at the perimeter
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in~ ("soc-scanner-01","tip-enrichment-01","recordedfuture-probe") and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("nessus.exe","qualys.exe","masscan.exe","nmap.exe","zgrab.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 - Triage: confirm the source IP/host is not a SOC scanner or TIP enrichment platform; pull all InitiatingProcessFileName / InitiatingProcessCommandLine + SHA1 for connections to the IP; check process ancestry for FireAnt Metakit (UC3) and SPECTRALVIPER hashes (UC2). Step 2 - Contain: network-isolate the device; collect memory + AutoRuns; revoke the AccountName's tokens; block all 8 OceanLotus C2 IPs at perimeter firewall regardless of this host. Step 3 - Hunt: extend the lookback to 18 months on this host and on any host sharing the same AccountName or same subnet; correlate to AAD signins from Vietnamese-IP geos; search file-share access logs for sensitive project / financial-regulator / Blazing Furnace investigation materials.
let OceanLotusIPs = dynamic(["139.162.11.152","142.91.98.77","139.180.128.42","139.99.33.239","166.88.77.186","103.119.47.104","38.60.245.37","194.68.26.241"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (OceanLotusIPs)
| extend HourBucket = bin(Timestamp, 1h), DayBucket = startofday(Timestamp)
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctHours = dcount(HourBucket),
            DistinctDays = dcount(DayBucket),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            Ports = make_set(RemotePort, 20),
            Processes = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 20),
            CmdSamples = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 10)
            by DeviceName, RemoteIP
| where DistinctDays >= 3 and DistinctHours >= 6
| extend CampaignSpanDays = datetime_diff('day', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| order by DistinctDays desc, CampaignSpanDays desc
let OceanLotusIPs = dynamic(["139.162.11.152","142.91.98.77","139.180.128.42","139.99.33.239","166.88.77.186","103.119.47.104","38.60.245.37","194.68.26.241"]);
union isfuzzy=true

| extend HourBucket = bin(TimeGenerated, 1h), DayBucket = startofday(TimeGenerated)

            by Src, Dst, User
| where DistinctDays >= 3 and DistinctHours >= 6
| extend CampaignSpanDays = datetime_diff('day', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| order by DistinctDays desc, CampaignSpanDays desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/

            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'

        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental
description: |

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Oracle PeopleSoft PSEMHUB exploitation (CVE-2026-35273) — inbound RCE traffic · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 callback to azurenetfiles.net masquerading as Azure Files · Network connections to article IPs / domains

Hunts inbound HTTP(S) requests to PeopleSoft web tier paths (/psp/, /psc/, /pls/, /psigw/, /PSEMHUB/) carrying gadget-chain or Java deserialization markers, paired with the named ShinyHunters source IPs from this campaign. ShinyHunters told BleepingComputer they chain zero-days + old PeopleSoft bugs and only some instances are vulnerable, so this targets the exploit traffic itself rather than the patch level. Rationale: Combines the 7 article-named ShinyHunters source IPs with the canonical Oracle PeopleSoft URI namespace (/psp/, /psc/, /psigw/, /PSEMHUB/) — the campaign signature BleepingComputer documents. Cross-checked Oracle PeopleSoft CPU advisories and prior ShinyHunters PeopleSoft writeups. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1037/ • https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/shinyhunters-claims-to-have-stolen-data-from-instructure-canvas/
ATT&CKT1190 T1203
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Oracle support engineer doing remote troubleshooting from a known IP
  • Pen-test firm running an authorized PeopleSoft assessment
  • Internal scanner (Tenable/Qualys) probing PeopleSoft URIs
  • Legitimate Java client integrations (PeopleSoft Integration Broker) from partners
  • Mobile-app campus portal sending large POST payloads
Suppression filter
| where not (cIP in (dynamic(["<known-pentest-ip>","<oracle-support-vpn-range>"])) )
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Pull the PeopleSoft web tier access log for the source IP and check whether the POST body contains serialized Java markers (rO0AB, ac ed 00 05) or known gadget-class names (CommonsBeanutils, CommonsCollections); inspect HTTP response status — exploitation usually triggers 500s before a success. 2) CONTAIN: Block the 7 campaign IPs at the perimeter/WAF, force a session invalidation on PSAPPSRV, and snapshot the PeopleSoft Application Server and integration gateway hosts. 3) HUNT: Pivot on the PSAPPSRV process tree for child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, java spawning shells), look for new local accounts in PSOPRDEFN, and search egress logs for any post-exploit beacons to azurenetfiles.net or the campaign /24.
let CampaignIPs = dynamic(["142.11.200.186","142.11.200.187","142.11.200.188","142.11.200.189","142.11.200.190","108.174.202.99","176.120.22.24"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where LocalPort in (8000, 8443, 8888, 443, 80)
| where RemoteIP in (CampaignIPs)
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("PSAESRV.exe","PSAPPSRV.exe","psadmin.exe","java.exe","tuxedo.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let CampaignIPs = dynamic(["142.11.200.186","142.11.200.187","142.11.200.188","142.11.200.189","142.11.200.190","108.174.202.99","176.120.22.24"]);
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem has_any ("/psp/","/psc/","/pls/","/psigw/","/PSEMHUB/","/integrationGateway")
| where csMethod == "POST" or csBytes > 5000
| where cIP in (CampaignIPs) or csUserAgent has_any ("Java/","python-requests","curl/")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus, csUserAgent, csBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc

C2 callback to azurenetfiles.net masquerading as Azure Files AICommand & Control High
Detects any DNS resolution or outbound connection to azurenetfiles.net — a typo-squat of the legitimate file.core.windows.net Azure Files namespace used by the ShinyHunters PeopleSoft campaign as a C2/exfil staging endpoint. The domain has no business purpose; any hit on a managed endpoint is high-fidelity. Rationale: azurenetfiles.net is the article's only named C2 domain — pre-extracted IOC. It typosquats Microsoft's legitimate Azure Files DNS (file.core.windows.net / *.azurefd.net) to blend into outbound traffic. Any hit is high-fidelity since there is no legitimate Microsoft service at this domain. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/files/storage-files-introduction • https://otx.alienvault.com/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / threat-intel analyst manually browsing the IOC
  • Sandbox detonation of a sample referencing the domain
  • Web-proxy preview/scanner pre-fetching the URL after an email scan
  • Newly onboarded host with stale browser bookmark from prior incident response
  • DNS over HTTPS resolver doing recursive lookup on behalf of another tenant
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe", "MpCmdRun.exe")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: For each hit, pull the initiating process, parent process and user — if the originator is PSAPPSRV/java/tuxedo on a PeopleSoft tier or any unmanaged process, treat as confirmed campaign activity. Capture the resolved IP and cross-check against the 7 known campaign IPs. 2) CONTAIN: Sinkhole azurenetfiles.net at internal DNS, block the resolved IP at the perimeter, isolate the host, and rotate credentials of any user session active on it. 3) HUNT: Search 30d back for any other host that resolved the domain, look for sibling typosquats (azureportals.net, microsoftazure-files.net), and validate PeopleSoft DB audit logs for bulk SELECT activity in the same window.
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteUrl has "azurenetfiles.net"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort),
(DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
  | where AdditionalFields has "azurenetfiles.net"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name endswith "azurenetfiles.net"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, IPAddresses=Result),
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery endswith "azurenetfiles.net"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Name=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryType, IPAddresses=DnsResponseName),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)

  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Name=DestinationHostName, QueryType="HTTP", IPAddresses=DestinationIP)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Outbound connections to ShinyHunters PeopleSoft campaign IP infrastructure AIActions on Objectives Medium
Alerts on any outbound TCP session from internal hosts to the 7 named ShinyHunters source IPs (142.11.200.186-190, 108.174.202.99, 176.120.22.24). These hit the exfil/staging tier — egress means data has likely already been staged. Rationale: Direct exact-IOC match on the 7 ShinyHunters infrastructure IPs pre-extracted from the article. No business reason for any internal host to talk to these endpoints — high-fidelity, low FP. Cross-checked against: • https://otx.alienvault.com/ • https://threatfox.abuse.ch/
ATT&CKT1041 T1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Incident-response analyst manually validating an IOC from a workstation
  • Threat-intel sandbox detonation
  • VPN client whose exit-node happens to share a /24 with one of these IPs
  • Outbound web proxy probe / health check
  • Researcher OSINT pivot in a browser
Suppression filter
| where Host !in ("<security-research-sandbox-host>")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: For each host, pull a 30-day timeline of connections to the IOC and identify total bytes sent — multi-GB egress within a short window indicates data exfiltration matching the 40GB ShinyHunters claim. Capture the initiating process and user. 2) CONTAIN: Block all 7 IPs at the perimeter, isolate the host, force-revoke any sessions/tokens from the identified user, and notify privacy/legal of potential mass PII egress. 3) HUNT: Cross-reference egress timing with PSAPPSRV / PeopleSoft DB query audit logs for bulk SELECTs against PS_PERSON / PS_STUDENT_REC / PS_BO tables. Search for archive utilities (7z/zip/tar) recently invoked on PeopleSoft hosts.
let CampaignIPs = dynamic(["142.11.200.186","142.11.200.187","142.11.200.188","142.11.200.189","142.11.200.190","108.174.202.99","176.120.22.24"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt")
| where RemoteIP in (CampaignIPs)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Connections=count(),
            BytesEstimate=countif(RemotePort in (80,443,8443))
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by FirstSeen desc
let CampaignIPs = dynamic(["142.11.200.186","142.11.200.187","142.11.200.188","142.11.200.189","142.11.200.190","108.174.202.99","176.120.22.24"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationIP in (CampaignIPs)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, SrcIp=SourceIP, DstIp=DestinationIP, DstPort=DestinationPort, App=ApplicationProtocol, Bytes=SentBytes, User=SourceUserName),
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)

  | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, DstIp=DstIpAddr, DstPort=DstPortNumber, App=NetworkApplicationProtocol, Bytes=NetworkBytes, User=SrcUsername)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Connections=count(), TotalBytes=sum(Bytes)
            by Host, SrcIp, DstIp, DstPort, App, User
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: Outbound Traffic to ShinyHunters PeopleSoft Campaign Infrastructure
id: 5b9d3e0c-7f24-4ed1-9c6e-2a8b5d1f3e74
description: Detects outbound network connections to the IPs used by the ShinyHunters extortion gang in the 2026 Oracle PeopleSoft data-theft campaign that hit the University of Nottingham.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nottingham-university-data-breach-affects-over-450-000-students/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1041
  - attack.t1071
logsource:
  category: network_connection
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationIp:
      - '142.11.200.186'
      - '142.11.200.187'
      - '142.11.200.188'
      - '142.11.200.189'
      - '142.11.200.190'
      - '108.174.202.99'
      - '176.120.22.24'
  condition: selection
level: high
@network.destination.ip:(142.11.200.186 OR 142.11.200.187 OR 142.11.200.188 OR 142.11.200.189 OR 142.11.200.190 OR 108.174.202.99 OR 176.120.22.24) OR @DestinationIp:(142.11.200.186 OR 142.11.200.187 OR 142.11.200.188 OR 142.11.200.189 OR 142.11.200.190 OR 108.174.202.99 OR 176.120.22.24)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ConnectionDirection=0
| RemoteAddressIP4=/^(142\.11\.200\.(186|187|188|189|190)|108\.174\.202\.99|176\.120\.22\.24)$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
| count > 0
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs (point at any VPC hosting PeopleSoft, identity, or corp egress)
fields @timestamp, srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort, protocol, bytes, packets, action
| filter dstAddr in ["142.11.200.186","142.11.200.187","142.11.200.188","142.11.200.189","142.11.200.190","108.174.202.99","176.120.22.24"]
      and action = "ACCEPT"
| stats count(*) as flows, sum(bytes) as totalBytes, min(@timestamp) as firstSeen, max(@timestamp) as lastSeen by srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort
| sort totalBytes desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
`summariesonly` | tstats count sum(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as total_bytes_out min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest IN ("142.11.200.186","142.11.200.187","142.11.200.188","142.11.200.189","142.11.200.190","108.174.202.99","176.120.22.24") AND All_Traffic.direction="outbound" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where firstTime>=relative_time(now(),"-30d")
summariesonly=false | tstats count sum(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as total_bytes_out min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest IN ("142.11.200.186","142.11.200.187","142.11.200.188","142.11.200.189","142.11.200.190","108.174.202.99","176.120.22.24") AND All_Traffic.direction="outbound" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where firstTime>=relative_time(now(),"-30d")
Bulk PeopleSoft student/finance table extract followed by external egress AIActions on Objectives Medium
Correlates large-result reads against PeopleSoft student-record tables (PS_PERSON, PS_PERS_DATA_EFFDT, PS_STUDENT_*) followed within 1 hour by multi-GB outbound transfers — the operational shape of the 40GB / 454,600-record breach claimed by ShinyHunters. Rationale: Article specifies 40GB / 454,600 records exfiltrated including names, passport numbers, fee payments — that data lives in PeopleSoft Campus Solutions tables (PS_PERSON, PS_PERS_DATA_EFFDT, PS_STDNT_CAR_TERM, PS_BI_HDR) and PSOPRDEFN. Pairing bulk DB read with multi-GB egress within 60min approximates the kill-chain step the article describes. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E92519_02/pshr92pbr29/eng/hcm/ccmn/CommonComponentsSchema.html
ATT&CKT1005 T1041 T1020
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Change.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Scheduled nightly data warehouse extract running outside business hours
  • University finance team running end-of-term billing reports
  • Backup job copying PeopleSoft DBs to off-site DR
  • Approved compliance/ICO data subject access request (DSAR) export
  • Integration job to Banner / Workday / SITS replicating student records
Suppression filter
| where User !in ("svc-banner-replication", "svc-dw-etl", "backupadmin")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Verify the bulk read was not from a known integration service account (look up the OPRID in PSOPRDEFN.OPRCLASS) and check whether the egress destination IP is in approved partners / Oracle Cloud OCI ranges or matches the campaign IPs. 2) CONTAIN: Suspend the DB user, revoke OAuth tokens for any linked PeopleSoft REST integration, and snapshot the PeopleSoft Application Server tier. 3) HUNT: Pivot on the OPRID across PSAUDIT and PSACCESSLOG for prior session activity, look back 60d for the first appearance of the user, and check for matching archive creation (7z/zip/tar) on the host within the same window.
let WindowMin = 60m;
let BulkEgress = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt")
    | where RemoteIPType == "Public"
    | summarize TotalConnections=count(),
                EgressBucket=bin(Timestamp, 15m)
                by DeviceName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, EgressBucket=bin(Timestamp, 15m)
    | where TotalConnections > 200;
let PSHosts = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("PSAESRV.exe","PSAPPSRV.exe","psadmin.exe","tuxedo.exe","sqlplus.exe")
       or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("PS_PERSON","PS_PERS_DATA_EFFDT","PS_STDNT_CAR_TERM","PSOPRDEFN","PS_BI_HDR","emplid","select * from ps_")
    | distinct DeviceName, BulkActivityTime=Timestamp;
BulkEgress
| join kind=inner PSHosts on DeviceName
| where EgressBucket between (BulkActivityTime - WindowMin .. BulkActivityTime + WindowMin)
| project EgressBucket, DeviceName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, TotalConnections, BulkActivityTime
let WindowMin = 60m;
let PSQueries = union isfuzzy=true
    (SecurityEvent
      | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
      | where EventID == 4688
      | where CommandLine has_any ("PS_PERSON","PS_PERS_DATA_EFFDT","PS_STDNT_CAR_TERM","PSOPRDEFN","PS_BI_HDR")
         or NewProcessName has_any ("PSAESRV.exe","PSAPPSRV.exe","sqlplus.exe")
      | project Host=Computer, BulkTime=TimeGenerated, User=Account, Cmd=CommandLine),
    (Syslog
      | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
      | where ProcessName has_any ("oracle","psaesrv","psappsrv")
      | where SyslogMessage has_any ("PS_PERSON","PS_PERS_DATA_EFFDT","PSOPRDEFN","PS_BI_HDR")
      | project Host=Computer, BulkTime=TimeGenerated, User="", Cmd=SyslogMessage);
let Egress = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DeviceAction =~ "allow"
    | summarize Bytes=sum(SentBytes), Sessions=count()
                by Host=SourceHostName, SrcIp=SourceIP, DstIp=DestinationIP, EgressBucket=bin(TimeGenerated, 15m)
    | where Bytes > 1073741824;
PSQueries
| join kind=inner Egress on Host
| where EgressBucket between (BulkTime - WindowMin .. BulkTime + WindowMin)
| project EgressBucket, Host, SrcIp, DstIp, Bytes, Sessions, BulkTime, User, Cmd
(source:(windows.security OR linux.auditd OR oracle.audit) AND (@CommandLine:(*PS_PERSON* OR *PS_PERS_DATA_EFFDT* OR *PSOPRDEFN* OR *PS_BI_HDR*) OR @process.command_line:(*PS_PERSON* OR *PS_PERS_DATA_EFFDT* OR *PSOPRDEFN* OR *PS_BI_HDR*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/(PSAESRV|PSAPPSRV|sqlplus|psadmin)\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/PS_(PERSON|PERS_DATA_EFFDT|STDNT_CAR_TERM|BI_HDR)|PSOPRDEFN/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName], function=count())
NETWORK

PeopleSoft host archives student-record directories prior to exfil AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects creation of large archive files (.zip, .7z, .tar.gz, .rar) by archive utilities on PeopleSoft application/DB tiers — the staging step before ShinyHunters' published 40GB archive. Filters on PS-tier hosts and archive names referencing student/finance keywords from the article (student, finance, billing, campus, portal). Rationale: Article confirms ShinyHunters shared 'an archive of allegedly stolen documents' totaling 40GB containing student finance / billing / payment / campus portal exports — those data domains map to PeopleSoft Campus Solutions/Finance modules. The archive-tool keyword overlap with article-cited data categories (student, finance, billing, campus, portal, passport) keeps FP rate manageable. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1560/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1074/001/
ATT&CKT1560.001 T1074.001

Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment

  • Backup tool compressing PS_HOME/PS_CFG_HOME before patching
  • Year-end finance archive job
  • Compliance team packaging records for a Subject Access Request
  • Penetration test artefact compression by red team
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !in~ ("svc-backup", "svc-veeam", "svc-commvault")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Inspect the archive's target path (FileEvents within ±5min on the same PID), confirm size and contents — multi-GB output is a strong indicator. Capture the user context and check whether the host is a PeopleSoft tier vs an admin workstation. 2) CONTAIN: Quarantine the archive file, suspend the user account, and isolate the host from the network. Force-revoke active Oracle DB sessions for that OPRID. 3) HUNT: Pivot 24h forward on the same host for the archive being uploaded to file.io / mega.nz / azurenetfiles.net / the campaign IPs, and search 30d back for any other archive activity by the same user across PeopleSoft tiers.

GitHub to Disable npm Install Scripts by Default to Stop Supply Chain Attacks

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 12 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

GitHub has announced what it said are "breaking changes" coming to npm version 12, one of which turns off install scripts by default to combat software supply chain threats. The changes aim to combat attack techniques that abuse the "npm install" command to trigger the execution of malicious code using npm lifecycle hooks. "Npm install" is used to download and install all the necessary

ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002 T1204.004 T1528

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Dependency Confusion or Typosquatting Installation · [LLM] npm registry traffic to non-allowlisted registry host during install · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — GitHub to Disable npm Install Scripts by Default to Stop Supply Chain Attacks
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm Post-Install Script Execution from Untrusted Package · [LLM] Suspicious npm Registry Authentication or Publish Activity · [LLM] Lateral Movement via Compromised Transitive Dependency · [LLM] npm pre/post-install Script Disabling Bypass Attempt
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
npm Post-Install Script Execution from Untrusted Package AIInstallation Medium
Detects child processes (PowerShell, cmd, bash, node) spawned by npm/node during install lifecycle hooks (preinstall/install/postinstall) — the exact code-execution surface GitHub is closing in npm 12. Flags developer or CI hosts where lifecycle scripts kick off interpreters, network egress tools, or implicit node-gyp rebuilds (binding.gyp). Rationale: Uses the article's explicit description of preinstall/install/postinstall lifecycle hooks as the npm code-execution surface, plus the named implicit node-gyp rebuild + binding.gyp path. Parent-child predicate is paired with suspicious child + cmdline content so it is not a bare 'powershell.exe' fire. Cross-checked against: • https://github.blog/changelog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/001/
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate native-module packages (sharp, sqlite3, node-sass, bcrypt) triggering node-gyp rebuild that shells out to cmd.exe
  • Internal devops scripts wrapping `npm install` in a PowerShell installer
  • CI runners (Jenkins, GitHub Actions runner) where npm install spawns bash/sh as the shell
  • Postinstall scripts that legitimately call curl/wget to fetch platform-specific binaries (e.g. Cypress, Puppeteer, Electron)
  • Yarn/pnpm wrappers invoking node.exe which spawns sh.exe on Windows for cross-platform script support
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","sharp","sqlite3","node-sass","bcrypt","puppeteer","cypress","electron") and FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","node-gyp.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the full process tree (npm.exe → child) and the package.json being installed (CWD of the npm.exe parent). Identify which package's lifecycle script ran (npm logs in %APPDATA%\npm-cache\_logs). 2) Contain — kill the child process, snapshot the host, remove the offending package from node_modules and quarantine the developer/CI cache. If a CI runner, revoke any tokens stored in that runner's environment. 3) Hunt — search org-wide for the same package@version in lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`), all hosts that ran the install in the last 30 days, and any outbound C2 connections from those hosts. Submit the package SHA to npm security and threat-intel feeds.

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm add","npm i ","node-gyp rebuild","binding.gyp")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("DownloadString","Invoke-WebRequest","IEX","-enc ","-EncodedCommand","http://","https://","FromBase64String","WebClient")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall","postinstall","node-gyp")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate

| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("DownloadString","Invoke-WebRequest","IEX","-enc ","-EncodedCommand","http://","https://","FromBase64String","WebClient")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall","postinstall","node-gyp")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| regex("(DownloadString|Invoke-WebRequest|IEX|-EncodedCommand|FromBase64String|WebClient|https?://)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Dependency Confusion or Typosquatting Installation AIDelivery Low
Hunts for npm install commands pulling packages from non-default registries or packages whose names closely resemble known organisational/internal prefixes — the dependency-confusion path that GitHub's --allow-remote default closure is partly aimed at. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit mention of --allow-git and --allow-remote becoming non-default in npm 12, plus git+/tarball dependency resolution paths. Excludes default registries to suppress baseline npm usage. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal artifact registries (Artifactory, Nexus, Verdaccio) configured via --registry
  • Forked GitHub repos pulled as direct git dependencies in monorepos
  • Yarn workspaces that legitimately resolve git+ssh dependencies
  • Local development against feature branches via `npm install github:org/repo#branch`
  • Lockfile-driven CI installs after intentional upgrade to a pre-release published as a tarball URL
Suppression filter
and not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("artifactory","nexus","verdaccio","jfrog","<your-internal-registry-hostname>"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the full command line and identify the package + registry/URL being installed. Cross-reference against the org's approved internal-registry list and the repo's package.json/package-lock.json. 2) Contain — if the registry/URL is unsanctioned, block at proxy/firewall, remove the package from the host, and rotate any npm tokens stored on that host. 3) Hunt — search lockfiles across all repos for the same registry/URL pattern, query DNS logs for the unsanctioned host, and inspect any CI pipelines using --allow-remote or --allow-git for unapproved sources.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--registry","--allow-remote","--allow-git","git+ssh://","git+https://","github:","gitlab:","bitbucket:")
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"https?://[^/\s]+\.tgz"
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("registry.npmjs.org","registry.yarnpkg.com","npm.pkg.github.com"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where ActingProcessName endswith "npm.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "npx.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "yarn.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "pnpm.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--registry","--allow-remote","--allow-git","git+ssh://","git+https://","github:","gitlab:","bitbucket:")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"https?://[^/\s]+\.tgz"
| where not (ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("registry.npmjs.org","registry.yarnpkg.com","npm.pkg.github.com"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: npm Install with Non-Default Registry or Remote URL Dependency
id: 9b2c5d8e-3f4a-4b6c-8d1e-2a3b4c5d6e7f
description: Detects npm/node/yarn/pnpm invocations using --registry, --allow-remote, --allow-git, or direct git+/tarball URLs — paths GitHub is closing by default in npm 12.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/github-to-disable-npm-install-scripts.html
author: SOC
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  npm_cli:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
  suspicious_args:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--registry'
      - '--allow-remote'
      - '--allow-git'
      - 'git+ssh://'
      - 'git+https://'
      - 'github:'
      - 'gitlab:'
  default_registry:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'registry.npmjs.org'
      - 'registry.yarnpkg.com'
      - 'npm.pkg.github.com'
  condition: npm_cli and suspicious_args and not default_registry
level: low
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\npx.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\NPM.exe) (@CommandLine:(*--registry* OR *--allow-remote* OR *--allow-git* OR *git+ssh* OR *git+https* OR *github:* OR *gitlab:*)) -@CommandLine:(*registry.npmjs.org* OR *registry.yarnpkg.com* OR *npm.pkg.github.com*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(npm|node|npx|yarn|pnpm)\.exe$/i
| regex("(--registry|--allow-remote|--allow-git|git\+ssh://|git\+https://|github:|gitlab:)", field=CommandLine)
| NOT regex("(registry\.npmjs\.org|registry\.yarnpkg\.com|npm\.pkg\.github\.com)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") (Processes.process="*--registry*" OR Processes.process="*https://*" OR Processes.process="*git+*" OR Processes.process="*github:*" OR Processes.process="*--allow-remote*" OR Processes.process="*--allow-git*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") (Processes.process="*--registry*" OR Processes.process="*https://*" OR Processes.process="*git+*" OR Processes.process="*github:*" OR Processes.process="*--allow-remote*" OR Processes.process="*--allow-git*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Suspicious npm Registry Authentication or Publish Activity AIInstallation Medium
Detects npm login/publish operations and .npmrc modifications that introduce or alter auth tokens — a signal of package-hijack staging or token theft in advance of malicious package republication. Rationale: Targets npm-CLI operations explicitly tied to registry auth/publish workflow (npm publish, npm login, token create) plus .npmrc file writes — the staging surface for the package-hijack scenario the article alludes to. Two correlated tables make the signal pivot-able. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/commands/npm-publish • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Maintainer workstations doing legitimate `npm publish` to internal registry
  • CI/CD runners publishing packages on tag-push (these should be allowlisted by host)
  • Developers running `npm login` once per quarter when tokens rotate
  • yarn/pnpm wrapper tools that write to .npmrc on `yarn config set` calls
  • npm version bump scripts that touch .npmrc to set always-auth=true
Suppression filter
and not (DeviceName in ("<known-ci-runner-1>","<known-ci-runner-2>") and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("runner.exe","agent.exe","jenkins.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — identify which package was being published, which auth token was used (~/.npmrc), and whether the host is an authorised maintainer/CI runner. Diff the published version against the source repo HEAD to spot timing gaps. 2) Contain — if unauthorised: revoke the npm token immediately (npm token revoke), unpublish/deprecate the suspect version, force-rotate any tokens in the .npmrc file. Block the host from the npm registry at the proxy. 3) Hunt — search for prior publishes from the same token, look at the host's process tree for token exfiltration (curl/wget reading .npmrc), and audit all packages owned by the affected maintainer account.
let PublishEvents = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm publish","npm login","npm adduser","npm token create","npm token revoke","--otp");
let NpmrcWrites = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName == ".npmrc"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$";
union PublishEvents, NpmrcWrites
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=coalesce(AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountName), FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let PublishEvents = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where ActingProcessName endswith "npm.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "npx.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm publish","npm login","npm adduser","npm token create","npm token revoke","--otp")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventType="PublishOrLogin";
let NpmrcWrites = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetFileName =~ ".npmrc"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, EventType="NpmrcWrite";
union PublishEvents, NpmrcWrites
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon ((@EventID:1 @Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\npx.exe OR *\\NPM.exe) @CommandLine:(*"npm publish"* OR *"npm login"* OR *"npm adduser"* OR *"npm token create"* OR *"npm token revoke"* OR *--otp*)) OR (@EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\.npmrc OR *\\.NPMRC)))
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(npm|node|npx)\.exe$/i regex("(npm publish|npm login|npm adduser|npm token (create|revoke)|--otp)", field=CommandLine)) OR (#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\\.npmrc$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe") (Processes.process="*npm publish*" OR Processes.process="*npm login*" OR Processes.process="*npm token*" OR Processes.process="*npm adduser*" OR Processes.process="*--otp*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe") (Processes.process="*npm publish*" OR Processes.process="*npm login*" OR Processes.process="*npm token*" OR Processes.process="*npm adduser*" OR Processes.process="*--otp*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Lateral Movement via Compromised Transitive Dependency AIInstallation Low
Hunts for execution of binaries dropped under node_modules/.bin/ or transitive node_modules paths spawning from unusual parents — the blast-radius path of a transitive-dependency compromise that npm 12's allowScripts default is intended to neutralise. Rationale: Pivot anchored on the node_modules path the article identifies as the transitive-execution surface (any dep can run code via install hooks). LOLBin + path filter is what differentiates ransomware/loader traffic from legit Node tooling.
ATT&CKT1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • esbuild/webpack/tsc/eslint binaries shelling out to cmd.exe to invoke platform helpers
  • node-gyp builds invoking cmd.exe → cl.exe under node_modules\node-gyp\
  • Cypress / Playwright launching browsers that spawn helper processes
  • Husky git hooks running bash.exe from node_modules\husky\
  • ESM resolver shims invoking node.exe from node_modules\.bin\
Suppression filter
and not (FolderPath has_any ("\\node_modules\\esbuild\\","\\node_modules\\webpack\\","\\node_modules\\.bin\\tsc","\\node_modules\\.bin\\eslint","\\node_modules\\husky\\","\\node_modules\\cypress\\","\\node_modules\\playwright\\","\\node_modules\\node-gyp\\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — identify the exact package (path under node_modules/<pkg>/) the binary executed from. Map to package.json + lockfile entry, capture version + integrity hash. Check npm advisory DB and ThreatFox for the package@version. 2) Contain — kill the process, isolate the host, remove node_modules and the lockfile entry, rotate any credentials/tokens the package might have read (env vars, .npmrc, ~/.aws/, ~/.ssh/). 3) Hunt — search all repos for the package@version in lockfiles, identify any CI/CD runner that installed it, and audit network egress from those hosts during the install window for C2 traffic.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has "\\node_modules\\"
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "\\node_modules\\"
| where FolderPath has_any ("\\node_modules\\.bin\\","\\node_modules\\")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","bash.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("DownloadString","Invoke-WebRequest","IEX","FromBase64String","-EncodedCommand")
   or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "\\node_modules\\" and FileName !in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","esbuild.exe","webpack.exe","tsc.exe","eslint.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where ActingProcessName has "\\node_modules\\" or ParentProcessName has "\\node_modules\\"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","bash.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("DownloadString","Invoke-WebRequest","IEX","FromBase64String","-EncodedCommand")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Suspicious Process Under node_modules Path
id: c4d6e8f0-1a2b-4c3d-9e5f-6a7b8c9d0e1f
description: Detects LOLBins or shells executing from inside a node_modules tree, or non-node binaries spawned by a node_modules executable — the blast surface of a compromised transitive npm dependency.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/github-to-disable-npm-install-scripts.html
author: SOC
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  in_node_modules:
    Image|contains: '\node_modules\'
  suspicious_lolbin:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
  condition: in_node_modules or (ParentImage|contains: '\node_modules\' and suspicious_lolbin)
level: low
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\node_modules\\* OR *\\NODE_MODULES\\*) OR @ParentImage:(*\\node_modules\\* OR *\\NODE_MODULES\\*)) (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe) OR @CommandLine:(*DownloadString* OR *Invoke-WebRequest* OR *-EncodedCommand* OR *FromBase64String*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| regex("\\\\node_modules\\\\", field=ImageFileName) OR regex("\\\\node_modules\\\\", field=ParentImageFileName)
| ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|bash|wscript|cscript|curl|wget|certutil|mshta|rundll32)\.exe$/i OR regex("(DownloadString|Invoke-WebRequest|IEX|FromBase64String|-EncodedCommand)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentImageFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_path="*\\node_modules\\*" (Processes.parent_process_name NOT IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","code.exe") OR Processes.process IN ("*powershell*","*cmd /c*","*-Command*","*curl *","*wget *")) by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_path="*\\node_modules\\*" (Processes.parent_process_name NOT IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","code.exe") OR Processes.process IN ("*powershell*","*cmd /c*","*-Command*","*curl *","*wget *")) by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
npm pre/post-install Script Disabling Bypass Attempt AIInstallation High
Detects developers/CI re-enabling the lifecycle-script execution path that npm 12 disables by default — e.g. `npm install --ignore-scripts=false`, `--foreground-scripts`, NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false, .npmrc `ignore-scripts=false`, or `npm approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending` invoked outside an approval workflow. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact prose: GitHub is closing --ignore-scripts/lifecycle-hook execution by default, and the documented re-enable path is the `approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending` workflow plus CLI flag/env overrides. .npmrc writes catch the persistent-config variant. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/commands/npm-install • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/
ATT&CKT1562 T1197
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Maintainer running `npm approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending` as part of GitHub-recommended upgrade workflow
  • Dev tooling installers (electron-builder, sharp postinstall) that legitimately require --foreground-scripts
  • CI runners reading NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS from a pipeline variable set by ops
  • Yarn migration scripts that touch .npmrc to set ignore-scripts=false during a controlled migration
  • Local dev sandbox environments where developers explicitly opt-in via env var
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending" and DeviceName in ("<known-maintainer-workstations>"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — confirm whether the host/user is going through the GitHub-recommended `npm approve-scripts` review (commit to package.json present) or is bypassing it interactively. Identify the package being installed when the bypass was set. 2) Contain — if unsanctioned, kill any in-flight install, revert .npmrc, unset env var, and quarantine node_modules. Force a clean `npm ci` with default settings. 3) Hunt — search the org for any other hosts/CI runners with the same env-var or .npmrc bypass, audit recent npm installs on those hosts for lifecycle-script execution (UC1 query), and check git history for unauthorised package.json `scripts` additions.
let CmdlineBypass = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--ignore-scripts=false","--foreground-scripts","approve-scripts","--allow-scripts-pending","NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false","npm_config_ignore_scripts=false","--scripts=true");
let NpmrcEnables = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName == ".npmrc"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$";
union CmdlineBypass, NpmrcEnables
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=coalesce(AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountName), FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let CmdlineBypass = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where ActingProcessName endswith "npm.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "npx.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "npm.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "node.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--ignore-scripts=false","--foreground-scripts","approve-scripts","--allow-scripts-pending","NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false","npm_config_ignore_scripts=false","--scripts=true")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventType="CmdlineBypass";
let NpmrcEnables = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName =~ ".npmrc"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, EventType="NpmrcModified";
union CmdlineBypass, NpmrcEnables
| order by TimeGenerated desc
